svg.title: Integrated MZI interleaver trees for the sixteen-lane Monarch shuffle
svg.desc: Sixteen input trees demultiplex sixty-four wavelengths per lane into sixteen residue groups. Leaf r carries wavelengths r, r+16, r+32 and r+48. Static waveguides connect input lane b, leaf r to output lane a=(b+r) mod 16, leaf r. Sixteen reverse trees multiplex the output lanes. An expanded four-level binary tree has one, two, four and eight unbalanced Mach-Zehnder interferometers. At a 100 GHz channel spacing the level delays are 5, 2.5, 1.25 and 0.625 picoseconds. Each elementary MZI has two couplers and unequal arms. The full elementary network has 480 MZIs, 960 couplers, 256 grouped links and eight MZIs traversed per signal. It uses fixed routing with slow phase trimming, not per-slot switching. Filter refinement, phase correction, footprint and power require device-level design.

g.text: The Monarch shuffle uses fixed MZI interleaver trees
Current design: 16 lanes × 64 wavelengths P(b, ℓ) = ((b + ℓ) mod 16, ℓ)
Example: input lane 3, leaf 5 [ℓ = 5, 21, 37, 53] → output lane 8, leaf 5
Wavelengths are preserved. Each output lane receives one residue group from each input lane.
Each level sorts the next bit of r = ℓ mod 16.
Fixed routing needs no per-slot switching. Flat-top filter refinement and phase correction can add components.
Functional connectivity only; this figure does not establish routed footprint, insertion loss or energy savings.
